contract: Editor hosts locate line-oriented fences, not full CommonMark or MDX syntax.
Markdown and MDX use the same rules; JSX and JavaScript expressions are not parsed.
Openers allow zero to three ASCII spaces, at least three backticks, tildes or colons, and an ASCII case-insensitive mermaid language followed by whitespace or end of line.
Closers use the same marker, at least the opening length, zero to three spaces of indentation and only trailing whitespace.

Whitespace before and after the language and after closing markers uses Unicode White_Space, matching Rust char::is_whitespace: U+0085 is whitespace and U+FEFF is not. Fence indentation still allows only ASCII spaces.
Non-Mermaid fences, including bare and colon fences, hide nested examples until a matching closer or EOF.
Outside fences, HTML comments run from literal <!-- through the next -->, without nesting; all transitions on each physical line are observed.
A line that starts inside a comment cannot open a fence, even when the comment ends on that line. Fence bodies and opening info strings do not change host comment state.
Unfinished Mermaid fences extend to EOF and count even with empty bodies. Unfinished comments and non-Mermaid fences hide later openers.

Rust preserves UTF-8 byte ranges and source line endings. Preview bodies normalize line endings and omit the newline immediately before a closing fence; empty previews are filtered after ordinal assignment.
